category: Runtime brand and design-token theming for a government collaboration workspace. Thematiq applies a government house style, expressed as NL Design System design tokens (and the French Cunningham/La Suite system), to a whole Nextcloud instance at runtime: every app, the login page, emails and the header, scoped per app or per group, with WCAG contrast evidence, a trial before publishing, an audit trail and OTAP portability. The buyer is a government IT or communications team that must make a self-hosted workplace look like the organisation's own. It therefore competes with the branding layer of other workplace suites (Nextcloud's own Theming app, Microsoft 365 organisational branding, openDesk) and with the design-token tooling a team uses to maintain a house style for government portals (Liferay DXP style books, Tokens Studio). It is not a design system or a component library: NL Design System, GOV.UK, USWDS and the like are its inputs, not its competitors.

capabilities.name: Define tokens as references to other tokens so one change flows through the semantic layer.

built.evidence: lib/Service/DesignTokensAliasResolver.php resolves W3C DTCG {token.path} aliases transitively (max 10 hops, cycle/missing-target detection) but ONLY during DTCG import: DesignTokensMapper.php:300-301 calls resolve() and writes the RESOLVED concrete value into the emitted CSS. Once stored, the app's own token editor and custom-overrides layer are flat --nldesign-*/--color-* custom properties with no alias graph, so editing one token afterwards does not cascade to anything that referenced it in the source document.
